reports.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales (delayed by Veterans Day)

outlook: Corn slipped to a fresh four-month low Monday, with December down 2¾ cents to about $4.38¾, as traders expect Tuesday's USDA WASDE report to raise world supplies and funds have flipped to a net short. Soybeans rose early on news the U.S. pressed China to buy more farm goods and that the U.S.-China trade truce was extended two months, but faded to close about 6¾ cents lower near $11.87 for January. Spring wheat gained 6 cents to $6.22 while Chicago wheat lost 3¼ cents to $5.88, with funds heavily short wheat ahead of a Russia–Ukraine summit set for Nov 10–11. ICE canola rose C$5.20 to C$757.40, while crude oil fell about 4%.
